_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for MSFT retrospectives (retro/build_msft.py). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date. A filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern; EDGAR gives only the filing date before 2002); every Microsoft earnings 8-K of the period was accepted after the close, with the 10-Q minutes apart. The builder uses the latest history vintage published by AS_OF, the prints published by AS_OF that report a fiscal year after that history (a Q4 print reports the year just ended and extends the history until the 10-K), the latest fiscal-year EPS range for the current year (its midpoint), the latest next-quarter revenue range (as growth on the year-ago quarter's revenue from its own filing), and the latest declared dividend. Microsoft's fiscal year ends on June 30. Values are as reported; a vintage takes each year from the latest 10-K that reports it, per share as published (the February 2003 two-for-one split restates the years published before it: 'eps_published', 'shares_published'), and a company figure excluding one-offs only replaces GAAP EPS (the history's 'normalization' says which). A print's margins and growth rates are derived from the raw figures of its release or the 10-Q filed with it ('raw'; the builder re-derives and checks them): the year-ago balance sheet comes from the year-ago quarter's own 10-Q or release, unearned revenue is short- plus long-term, and a comparable operating income replaces GAAP only when the release gives it for both quarters and it excludes only one-offs. Guides start with the Q4 FY07 release (the Q3 FY07 release's preliminary fiscal 2008 range is superseded before any built date). rule_t holds the annual values behind the engine's signal thresholds. Edit only to add newly published facts or fix a transcription error against the cited filing.

rule_t._doc: Rule T values behind the engine's signal thresholds (retro/README.md, 'MSFT'): the ten annual values FY1998-FY2007 (the decade of the FY2007 10-K, the vintage public on 2008-01-04). Revenue growth from the five-year summary of the latest 10-K published by then that reports both years; the margins from the income statements of the latest 10-K that reports both years; unearned revenue (short- and long-term) and the receivables gap within each year's own 10-K (its two balance sheets and its income statement). A company figure excluding one-offs replaces the reported one where it was published for both years on the same basis: FY2006 and FY2007 operating income as adjusted ($17,581M and $19,735M, Q4 FY07 release). Everything else as reported, seams included (the FY1999 revenue-recognition restatement of FY1997-FY1998 revenue and cost of revenue, the SFAS 123 restatement of FY2002-FY2003, reclassifications between 10-Ks).
